test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 05 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is responsible for attending to disputes concerning recruitment and conditions of service of public personnel at the Centre?
solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Central Administrative Tribunal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Central Administrative Tribunal****​**

 
 
• The **Central Administrative Tribunal** was set on 1 November 1985 by the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985.

 
 
• The Central Administrative Tribunal deals with service matters about the Central Government employees or of any Union Territory, or local or other government under the control of the Government of India, or of a corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government.
 
• The ​Central Administrative Tribunal consists of a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and members.
 
• Members are from both judicial as well as administrative streams.
 
• The **Central Administrative Tribunal** has 17 regular benches.
 
• 15 benches operate at the principal seats of High Courts and from the remaining two each one at Lucknow and Jaipur.
 
• These Benches also hold circuit sittings at other seats of the High Courts.
 
• Tribunal is a Quasi-judicial body.
 
 
• 
• Tribunals have the power to try cases of special matters which are conferred on them by statutes. The Tenure, terms, and conditions of the services of the members of the Administrative Tribunal are entirely in the hands of the Executive.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Joint Administrative Tribunal**

 
 
• **​**​It means an Administrative Tribunal for two or more States established under the **Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985.**
 
• A Joint Administrative Tribunal for two or more States shall exercise all the jurisdiction, powers and authority exercisable by the **Administrative Tribunals for such States.**
 
 
 
• **The Settlement and Appellate Tribunal**
 
 
• **​**The Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal established under section 14 of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997 (24 of 1997), shall, on and from the commencement of Part XIV of Chapter VI of the Finance Act, 2017 (7 of 2017).
 
• Be the Appellate Tribunal for this Act and the said Appellate Tribunal shall exercise the jurisdiction, powers, and authority conferred on it by or under this Act.
 
• Under X chapter of the Information Technology Act, 2000 the provisions of the Appellate Tribunal are given.
 
 
 
• **The Competition Appellate Tribunal**
 
 
• The commission was established on 14 October 2003. It became fully functional in May 2009 with Dhanendra Kumar as its first chairman.
 
• Established by the Government of India under the Competition Act, 2002 for the administration, implementation, and enforcement of the Act.
 
• It is the chief national** competition** regulator in India.
 
• It is a Statutory Body within the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
 
• CCI consists of a Chairperson and 6 Members appointed by the Central Government.
 
• The Commission must eliminate practices hurting competition, promote and sustain competition, protect the interests of consumers and ensure freedom of trade in the markets of India.**​**
